headline: Evolution is gradual change through selection—what works survives, what doesn't disappears
universal_truth: Change happens whether you guide it or not; conscious evolution beats unconscious drift
fun_facts: Humans share 50% of their DNA with bananas—all life evolved from common ancestors
Evolution continues today—bacteria evolving antibiotic resistance is evolution in real-time
Human brains evolved for environments that no longer exist—we're running ancient software in modern conditions
discussion_questions: How have you evolved as a person over time?
What behaviors served you once but no longer do?
How can you consciously guide your own evolution?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Every living thing is related. Trace your ancestry far enough back and you share grandparents with every creature—fish, trees, bacteria. Life changes gradually over time, accumulating small differences until new forms emerge. Evolution is the slow sculptor of all life.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Evolution isn't just biology—it's a pattern. Ideas evolve, cultures evolve, you evolve. What drives this gradual change, and can we guide it?

options.text: Evolution works through variation and selection—differences emerge, and what fits the environment survives to reproduce, gradually shaping the population
options.response: Yes. Evolution has no goal, only a process: vary, select, repeat. What works propagates; what doesn't disappears. Understanding this process lets you apply it consciously.

options.text: Evolution moves toward improvement and progress
options.response: Evolution has no direction—just fit to current environment. 'Better' only means 'fits better now'...

q1.title: Variation and Selection
q1.script: Evolution needs two things: variation (differences between individuals) and selection (some variants survive better than others). Without variation, no change. Without selection, no direction. Both are necessary.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Variation and Selection"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: No Destination
q2.script: Evolution has no goal—it's not 'trying' to create anything. What fits survives; what doesn't, doesn't. 'Advanced' just means 'well-suited to current conditions.' When conditions change, 'advanced' can become extinct.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Evolution
q3.script: You evolve too—habits change, beliefs update, skills develop. The question is whether you evolve consciously or drift unconsciously. You can apply evolutionary thinking: try variations, keep what works, discard what doesn't.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Change happens whether you guide it or not. Conscious evolution beats unconscious drift. Try, select, repeat—deliberately.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 212—the last day of July! Tomorrow, we start August with extinction. Until then, identify a behavior you could experimentally vary.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Conscious Evolution - Try a Variation
growTrack.activity: Pick a routine or behavior you do automatically. Try a small variation this week—different approach, different timing, different method. Notice what works better. This is conscious evolution: vary, select, repeat.
